stage_a.note: Founders are highly energetic, smiling constantly, and use enthusiastic gestures throughout the presentation.
Loud, passionate delivery with continuous engaged excitement about their product and its features.
Very friendly and approachable, frequently smiling and engaging directly with the panel.

venture.description: Semi-sweet cocktail wines with higher alcohol content and natural fruit extracts.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Introduces herself as Whitney Gates.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces himself as Chaz Gates.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States they are from Dallas, Texas.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States their ask of one hundred eighty-five thousand dollars for an eight percent stake.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Describes the problem of boring wines and time-consuming craft cocktails.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Mentions the desire for convenient ready-to-drink options without fake ingredients.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Playfully scolds Chaz and asks the sharks for a drumroll.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Introduces Wondry, a collection of wines infused with organic fruit extracts.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Highlights the thirteen point nine percent alcohol by volume.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the wines blur the lines between premium wine and craft cocktails.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Notes they are aged in small batches and tastefully crafted for any occasion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they reject exclusivity within the wine industry.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Mentions they are part of the less than one percent of Black American winemakers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks the sharks if they are ready to shatter glass ceilings with Wondry.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Proposes a toast to sip different.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains the different wine varieties while the investors taste them.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Comments that the watermelon rose tastes amazing.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Thanks Daymond for the compliment.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: States that he likes the apple flavor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that the apple flavor is good.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains that their wines have double the alcohol content of average semi-sweet wines.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if they are under the typical fourteen ninety-nine price point for wine.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States their suggested retail price is eighteen ninety-nine due to premium organic ingredients.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if they sell direct to consumer or through retail.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms they do both and are selling in two big box retailers.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks which big box retailers they are in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Names Target and Total Wine as their retailers.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what it costs to manufacture one bottle.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States it costs three dollars and sixty-one cents to make and sells for thirteen thirty wholesale.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Praises the margin.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Notes the good margin and asks when they started the business.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States they started in August twenty twenty-one, eleven months ago.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what their sales have been in those eleven months.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Reports two hundred and fifty thousand dollars in sales.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Comments that the sales figure is not bad.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks what their profit was on the two hundred and fifty thousand.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: States they made sixty thousand in profit, a thirty-two percent operating margin.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Comments that the profit margin is also not bad.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how much of their own money they have invested.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they invested one hundred thousand dollars from their savings.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks about their previous history and if they were winemakers.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Explains she grew up watching her paralyzed uncle make wine in his garage.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Jokes that her uncle was a bootlegger.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Laughs and agrees with Mark's joke.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Continues that her uncle inspired her, and she taught herself and took collegiate courses.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks Chaz to share his personal story.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Details his journey from a single-parent home to becoming a corporate lawyer and in-house counsel.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Jokes that Chaz has underachieved in his life.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Laughs at Peter's joke.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if they have started talking to Costco.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Says they haven't talked to Costco yet but have engaged Target and Total Wine.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Interrupts to ask if they are actually on the shelf in Target.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Confirms and adds they are the number two Black-owned adult beverage brand nationwide.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: States he doesn't know anything about wine and exits the deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Explains she avoids sugar and wouldn't drink it, so she exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Shares his past difficult experience owning a wine business and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what they need the investment money for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains they need to invest in an automatic bottling line to be more efficient.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks if they own all their own equipment and do their own bottling.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms they do it all themselves and emphasizes their hard work and passion.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: States he would want his own wine business if he invested more time, and exits.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Offers two hundred thousand dollars for fifteen percent equity.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Counters Mark's offer, asking for two hundred and fifty thousand for fifteen percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Revises his offer to two hundred and twenty-five thousand for fifteen percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts Mark's revised offer enthusiastically.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Hugs the founders and expresses excitement about the local deal.

decisions.note: Doesn't know anything about wine, hopes someone else does.
Stays away from sugar, won't drink it herself, so not a good investment for her.
Owned a wine business before, thinks it's a tough journey, not right for him.
If he invests more time and resources into wine, it will be in his own business.
Offers more money for more equity to make the numbers easier.
Counters with a higher amount for the same equity.
Meets in the middle on the amount.

record.notes: The founders alternate rapidly during the prepared presentation, resulting in many short turns.
